episodes.212498: A slow moving upper level disturbance over northern Mexico and the Desert Southwest combined with moist surface southeast flow resulting in thunderstorm development across central and eastern New Mexico during the afternoon and evening hours. Some storms resulted in severe hail at Chacon, severe thunderstorm wind gusts near Sumner Lake and Endee on June 2nd and some burn scar flash flooding in Ruidoso on June 3rd.
episodes.212565: Several clusters of severe thunderstorms tracked across portions of central and northeast South Dakota during the late afternoon and evening hours of June 3, generating high winds, large hail, and heavy rainfall.  ||One cluster tracked along the North Dakota border, where a personal weather station in Frederick recorded a peak wind gust of 84 mph. These high winds destroyed the football field scoreboard and a storage shed in Frederick, knocked down trees and a radio tower, downed power lines in Hecla, and snapped power poles and flipped an irrigation pivot six miles north of Britton. The city of Britton lost electrical power. Three additional weather stations in Marshall County clocked wind gusts in excess of 60 mph. ||A second storm cluster moved out of eastern South Dakota into the southern Glacial Lakes region. Quarter-sized hail occurred at several locations. Heavy rainfall topping out at 4.40 inches in Clear Lake resulted in water six inches deep running over roads and caused a creek near the golf course to overflow its banks. Across central South Dakota, storms produced hail ranging from penny to golf ball size south of Interstate 90.
episodes.212568: Two distinct clusters of severe thunderstorms impacted central and northeast South Dakota during the afternoon and evening of June 4. In the northeast, severe storms generated large hail up to golf ball size five miles south-southeast of Cottonwood Lake and nine miles southeast of Tulare. The Huron Remote Automated Weather Station (RAWS) 12 miles east-southeast of Sunshine Bible Academy recorded a peak wind gust of 86 mph.||A separate cluster of storms tracked through mainly central and south central South Dakota producing peak wind gusts of 71 mph and 68 mph at the South Dakota Department of Transportation Road Weather Information System (RWIS) stations six miles southwest of the Joe Creek Recreation Area and nine miles north-northwest of Vivian, respectively.
episodes.212596: Scattered severe storms impacted north central and northeast Kansas on June 4th with wind damage including a short lived but strong tornado that developed over the community of Riley and moved northeast for approximately 4-5 miles.  It produced EF2 damage with winds to around 120 mph at one home just northeast of Riley.  No injuries were reported.
episodes.212855: Isolated thunderstorms developed early in the afternoon of the fourth along an old outflow boundary from convection the previous day. A very moist and unstable atmosphere allowed one of these storms to become severe as it moved over northwestern Hall County producing severe wind gusts for ten minutes.
episodes.213269: A couple of different rounds of thunderstorms brought heavy rain to portions of the headwaters of the Big Sioux River. This heavy rain resulted in the upper portions of the Big Sioux rising above flood stage for a short period.
episodes.213432: Widely scattered strong to severe storms impacted portions of south-central Kansas during the early afternoon hours of June 4th. A microburst at I-235 and Central Avenue caused minor structural damage with wind gusts estimated to be up to 85 mph. This included downing transmission lines which stopped traffic on 235. Other storms around the area produced around 60 to 65 mph wind gusts.
episodes.213598: A few late evening thunderstorms developed across the Dakotas and moved eastward along a sharp gradient of mixed layer instability. In extreme western MN, sub-severe thunderstorms became more numerous given a diminishing environment for severe storms. However, one storm which had crossed into Yellow Medicine County briefly pulsed up enough to produce a 61mph wind gust at the Canby Airfield. This brief episode of wind did down a couple of trees in Canby as well as damage two empty grain bins just SE of Canby along Hwy 68.
episodes.213744: Showers and thunderstorms affected the combined Panhandles each afternoon and evening in the early parts of June. With enough moisture, instability and sources to provide atmospheric lift, these storms were able to become severe each day and bring large hail to the region. A few instances of damaging winds and flooding also occurred.
episodes.213793: An outflow boundary moved into Lea County during the pre-dawn hours of the 4th, with showers and thunderstorms developing along it as it did so. Storms developed and sat over Highway 18 between Hobbs and Lovington, which resulted in flash flooding on the highway. Convection dissipated later that morning, but additional showers and thunderstorms developed later in the afternoon of the 4th.
episodes.213794: During the afternoon of the 4th, an upper-level trough was moving in from the west. Synoptic lift ahead of this feature, coupled with upslope flow and some lift from decaying outflow, allowed showers and thunderstorms to develop in/around the higher terrain and in western portions of the Permian Basin. Convection tended to move slowly and produce heavy rainfall during the evening and into the early morning hours of the 5th. As a result, flash flooding was reported in Gaines and Pecos Counties.
episodes.214598: A deep upper-level trough moved along the international border with a strengthening southerly flow of moisture and instability into southeast South Dakota. With the terminus of the transport near the mid-James River Valley, isolated storms developed by very late afternoon with strong updrafts and large hail up to ping-pong ball size. A more linear system developed along the dry line in central South Dakota during the early evening and produced damaging wind gusts up to 70 mph near and south of Interstate 90.
episodes.214601: Leftover boundaries from June 3 thunderstorms and diurnally driven MLCAPE up to 1500-2000 J/kg triggered rapid storm development in the mid-James River Valley by mid-to-late afternoon. These storms intensified due to 40-45 kts of effective shear, producing hail as large as baseballs.
episodes.215001: A few strong to severe thunderstorms produced low end severe weather across the Black Hills.
episodes.215472: Scattered thunderstorms produced isolated large hail and localized flash flooding across the eastern half of the area.
episodes.215593: Southeast surface flow brought 50s dew points into the Rio Grande Valley.  Weak south-southwest flow aloft kept storm motion slow but did provide enough shear for some severe thunderstorm wind gusts to occur.

events.narrative: The Emergency Manager reported trees and power lines down 6 miles north of the city of Britton. An irrigation pivot was flipped over during the storm. Britton lost power due to  the damage to powerlines.
A member of the public estimated winds of 60 mph with the storm.
A trained spotter noted hail damage to crops 3 to 4 miles south of Castlewood.
Thunderstorm winds gusts measured by South Dakota Mesonet station ACMS2 3 miles north-northwest of Academy.
The Malone Mesonet site on the White Sands Missile Range recorded a peak gust of 62 mph.
Thunderstorm wind gusts measured by South Dakota Mesonet station WTES2 near White Lake.
Thunderstorm winds gusts measured by the South Dakota Road Weather Information System site near Plankinton.
The Condron Field Mesonet site on the White Sands Missile Range reported a peak gust of 63 mph.
Thunderstorm wind gusts measured by the South Dakota Mesonet station VNMS2 at Mount Vernon.

Most arroyos and low water crossings in the Talavera area ran overnight, particularly the arroyo and crossing on Soledad Canyon Road just east of Alma Road.  This area was likely impassable at the peak flow.  Nearby driveway with culverts was washed out.
Law enforcement reported downed tree branches blocking a road in Canby.

Flooding and standing water was observed at a horse farm south of Mesilla Diversion Dam around midday 6/4.  Outbuildings, stables and livestock were surrounded by muddy water.  Time of flooding estimated.
Two empty grain bins had their sides blown from a strong thunderstorm wind gust. The AWOS station located at the Canby Municipal Airport measured a 53kt thunderstorm wind gust.
Thunderstorm wind gusts measured by a personal weather station.

Six inches of water was observed running over and along Parkway Drive on the south side of Clear Lake. Water in the creek had also topped its bank on the southwest side of the road adjacent to the golf course.  A resident in Clear Lake recorded 4.40 inches of moisture with the system.

Post from the Chaves County Sheriff's office showed water in the normally dry Long Arroyo going across State Highway 249 near mile marker 6, prompting a road closure. Water appeared to be slow-moving with the overall depth at the time unknown.

Emergency management reported standing water on Highway 18 between Lovington and Hobbs. The total time of occurrence is estimated from radar and from the time of the initial report. No damage was reported.

Big Sioux River near Estelline rose above flood stage the morning of June 4th, cresting around 1.95 feet above flood stage (1645.95 feet) on June 5th. This crest is in the Moderate category. The river then fell below flood stage on the morning of June 7th.
A Texas Tech University West Texas mesonet site near Lesley measured severe wind gusts from 1138 CST through 1148 CST. A peak gust of 65 mph was measured at 1146 CST.

There were several power poles that were knocked down and leaning with power lines laid out across I-235. There were also several tree limbs down; however, there was minimal damage to nearby homes. Over 7000 people were without power as a result of the damage.
Estimated wind gusts were around 50 to 60 mph.
The mesonet located one mile east-northeast of Mclean first measured a severe wind gust of 63mph at 1327. The peak wind gust was 67mph which was measured at 1330.

A trained spotter along State Highway 4 at mile marker 40 near the Valles Caldera Preserve entry observed penny size hail with overall accumulations just under an inch deep from a strong thunderstorm.
Photo showed hail of various size from golf ball to baseball size.
Wind gusts were estimated to be around 60 mph.
There were several large tree limbs blown down in Mulvane.
Wind gusts were estimated to be between 50 and 60 mph.
Tree limb down on power line, causing the downed power line.
Damage to a homestead of unknown severity.  Emergency Manager determined to be from damaging winds.

Pecos Fire Department relayed a delayed report of flash flooding by the old sulfur mine near the Reeves/Culberson County line. A truck was immobilized by flood waters. The time of occurrence is estimated from radar. The cost of damages is also estimated.

NWS damage survey revealed a tornado developed over the small community of Riley and tracked around 4 miles to the northeast.  The tornado caused EF2 damage at one home just northeast of Riley where outbuildings were destroyed and trees suffered significant damage.  The rest of the track was EF0 to at worst low end EF1 damage.  No property loss data was available as of this report.
Spotter called in hail report.
Quarter size and slightly larger hail with the 1st round, then the second round was about  dime size.
Golf ball-sized hail was reported nine miles southeast of Tulare.
Photo via social media, time estimated based on radar.
Spotter called in hail report.
